clue.text: Bird settled by musician buying instrument?

definitions.meaning: a large tropical bird with a huge curved beak topped by a casque
read literally, the invoice a player pays when purchasing a brass instrument

explanation.surface: A bird appears to be paid for by a performer shopping for gear.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a whimsical reading: a horn bill would be the account a musician settles after buying a horn.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a family of tropical birds famous for their oversized beaks.

clue.text: Tax excessively — that's how our government rules English

parts.note: a government rules over us, so the phrase supplies the words over us

explanation.surface: A complaint that the state overtaxes the people, illustrated by English rule.
explanation.definitionFit: To tax something excessively is to strain or wear it out through too much use.

clue.text: Crossword clues are in order like this

definitions.text: Crossword clues are in order like this

parts.words: Crossword clues are in order like this
parts.note: clues in a puzzle are listed by their grid numbers, ascending, so the sequence is by figures

explanation.surface: A remark on how puzzle clues are arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordering by number is the arrangement that counts upward one, two, three.

clue.text: Daughter employed in so-called architect's plant

indicators.note: the daughter is put to work inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Inigo Jones was the English architect, known by his first name here

explanation.surface: A daughter works at a factory belonging to a self-styled architect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory but is a dye plant. Inigo Jones (1573-1652) was a celebrated English architect.
explanation.definitionFit: The dye-producing shrub Indigofera gives its name to the deep blue dye.

clue.text: Deliberately ignore appearance in alternative fashion

parts.note: a look is someone's appearance
done another way, the opposite manner

explanation.surface: A fashion critic dismisses a look in favour of a different style.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to avert one's gaze so as to pretend not to notice wrongdoing.

clue.text: One may be downtrodden in Oxford

definitions.text: One may be downtrodden in Oxford

parts.words: One may be downtrodden in Oxford
parts.note: an Oxford is a laced shoe; the lining inside it is stood on all day

explanation.surface: Someone oppressed in the university city.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford suggests the university city, but an Oxford is also a style of laced shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner sole of a shoe is literally trodden down by the wearer's foot.

clue.text: Mischievously intimate about his misbehaving

indicators.note: the verb wraps round the other piece, as 'about' means surrounding

parts.note: to intimate is to imply or hint

indicators.note: the letters of the word his behave badly and fall out of order

explanation.surface: Someone hints playfully at a man's bad conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting like a little devil or imp means behaving with playful naughtiness.

clue.text: Mineral oil 'freely distributed over plant

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second
the letters of oil are scattered about loosely and rearranged

parts.note: a vine is a climbing plant

explanation.surface: Mineral oil is liberally spread over a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'over' means the first piece sits above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivine is a green silicate of magnesium and iron, a common rock-forming mineral.

clue.text: Refreshments found in team's quarters

parts.note: a cricket or football team is an eleven, here with its possessive
E and S, east and south, are two of the compass quarters

explanation.surface: Snacks are discovered in the players' living quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' are points of the compass, not lodgings. In Britain a mid-morning snack is called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the British term for a light snack and tea taken around eleven in the morning.

clue.text: Broadcast live beside a large inland sea

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
the Med, short for Mediterranean, is a sea almost enclosed by land

explanation.surface: Something is transmitted live from beside the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' is a past tense meaning sent out, as rays of light are.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmit a signal is to send it out in a directed ray.

clue.text: Suitable with nothing for a change? Just the reverse

indicators.note: one letter, the a, is exchanged for another, so the word is altered by swapping

parts.note: apposite means suitable or apt
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A suggestion to swap a fitting choice for nothing, then a retort reversing that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' swaps the A of APPOSITE for O, nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrary in every way is what is meant by the phrase about reversal.

clue.text: Unconditional claim not allowed at first

indicators.note: the ruled-out piece is placed in front, coming earlier than the other

parts.note: out means ruled out, not permitted
a right is a claim or entitlement

explanation.surface: A claim is rejected from the start without conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Something complete and without reservation is total and absolute.

clue.text: Band beginning to sail East on tour

indicators.note: in an across clue, putting one thing on another places it after, so East follows tour
only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: a trip is a tour or journey

explanation.surface: A musical group begins sailing eastward on a concert tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians but means a strip of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow strip of colour on a surface is a band.

clue.text: Pass in reading, writing, or arithmetic set by a head

parts.note: these are the three Rs of basic schooling, so any one of them is R
per head, or a head, means each

explanation.surface: Getting through one of the three basic school subjects headed by a teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'three Rs' is a British phrase for basic education: reading, writing and arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach something to someone is to hand it over, as in passing the salt.

clue.text: Cabinet-maker's new deal

parts.note: a prime minister forming a cabinet redistributes posts, and a card dealer mixes the pack again

explanation.surface: A furniture craftsman makes a fresh arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cabinet is the senior ministers of a government; the prime minister moves them around.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearrangement of ministerial posts is likened to mixing the cards for another deal.

clue.text: Man and woman recently signed up for union

definitions.text: Man and woman recently signed up for union

parts.words: Man and woman recently signed up for union
parts.note: a couple who have just joined in marriage, not workers joining a trade union

explanation.surface: Two people have just joined a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests a trade union but means marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple who have just been married are the recently wed pair.

clue.text: Gloss over a series of defeats

definitions.meaning: to cover up faults, conceal unpleasant facts
in sport, a series lost without winning a single game

explanation.definitionFit: Lime paint covers blemishes, hence concealing; in sport it also means a total drubbing.

clue.text: Charge a large number entering vessels together

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, so it is placed inside

parts.note: to charge a glass is to fill it
a lot is a large number

explanation.surface: A fee is charged for many entering boats together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts LOT inside FILLA, after its F.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleet of small ships sailing as a group is a small fleet.

clue.text: Coarse material for the royals

parts.note: royals are the sails set above the topgallants on a square-rigged ship, so heavy canvas for them

explanation.surface: Rough fabric is supplied to the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'royals' looks like the royal family but are sails high on a ship's mast.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy canvas used for making ship's sails is the stuff in question.

clue.text: I am going to pond to catch a set-end duck

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'I am going to pond to catch a set-end duck': IM + MER(S)E needs S, but 'set-end' gives T; probably OCR of "set's end", which the check will not take as a correction
annotationWithheld.clue: I am going to pond to catch a set-end duck

clue.text: Supports a man fellows heard about

indicators.note: what is spoken of is heard, so the sound of the word is used

parts.note: peers are one's fellows or equals

explanation.surface: A man backed by friends who have heard of him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a man' is a second pointer: Piers is a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Pillars bearing a bridge or arch hold it up.

clue.text: Achieve redemption as a sort of miracle

indicators.note: a variety of the word, its letters rearranged into another sort

explanation.surface: Salvation is achieved through a kind of miracle.
explanation.definitionFit: To win back or redeem something is to recover it.

clue.text: Greeting sailor involved in act of piracy

parts.note: hi is a greeting
Jack, or Jack Tar, is a traditional name for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor waves hello while taking part in piracy.
explanation.definitionFit: The seizure of a vehicle or vessel by force is modern piracy.

clue.text: Greatest sum to free before closing of account

indicators.note: the anagram comes ahead of the final letter
the letters are set loose and rearranged
only the final letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: The biggest amount freed up before an account is closed.
explanation.definitionFit: The utmost is the greatest or most extreme degree.

clue.text: Working classes featured in one show or another

indicators.note: appearing within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to evince is to show or display
D and E are the lowest social grades in British market research, the working classes

explanation.surface: The working classes are featured in a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: D and E are the British social-grade labels for manual workers and the poorest. 'another' is a second word meaning show, as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof or testimony is a show of facts; the clue says it is a second word for show.

clue.text: Superfluous ornament underneath coat, originally

parts.note: an animal's fur is its coat
below means underneath

explanation.surface: Fancy trim is hidden underneath a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' is a nod: the pieces read in the clue's order would be below fur, so the coat comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A furbelow is a flounce or showy frill on clothing.

clue.text: In Turkey, mount paintings a painter dropped in

indicators.note: the painter falls inside the paintings, so one piece goes within

parts.note: art means paintings
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: A painter drops in on a show of paintings in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Ararat is the mountain in eastern Turkey where Noah's ark is said to have rested.

clue.text: Female adviser rejected passion in mature years

indicators.note: thrown back, so the whole construction is read backwards
the passion goes inside the years

parts.note: age means mature years
ire is anger, a passion

explanation.surface: A woman counsellor rejects passion in later life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns round the whole container, not just the passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Egeria was the nymph who counselled King Numa; her name means any woman mentor.

clue.text: Port's okay, oddly, when eating old meat

indicators.note: the outer letters swallow the others, so they go inside
the letters are arranged in an odd way, an anagram

parts.note: ham is a meat

explanation.surface: A port wine tastes fine, curiously, when served with old meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the wine; it is a harbour city, and 'oddly' is the anagram signal, not a pick of odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Yokohama is a major Japanese seaport near Tokyo.
